title: Authoring Alias Table
description: Maps author-side spellings to canonical V3.1 effect identifiers and parameter envelopes. One alias-table file per axis (transition, filter, shader, sampler, mask, style). The canonicalize function consults this table when it encounters {<axis>: "<from>", ...} in the shorthand input. Adding rows here is a versionless change — it does not bump the V3.1 contract.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor tooling. Optional.

version.description: Alias-table format version. Bumps independently of the canonical schema.

axis.description: Which authoring axis this table covers. The canonicalizer keys off this when routing shorthand.

from.description: Author-side spelling. lowerCamelCase is canonical; the canonicalizer also accepts snake_case via case-insensitive lookup. Names must be unique within a table.

canonicalEffect.description: Canonical effect identifier as it appears in graph node 'effect' field (e.g., 'filter.dim', 'shader.focused_row_gradient', 'mask.iris').

paramMapping.description: Maps author-side parameter names to canonical input field names with envelope hints. Parameters not listed here pass through with the same name and type-inferred envelope (see common/canonicalization-rules.json).

defaultParams.description: Canonical-side input fields that always apply unless explicitly set on the author side. Values are pre-canonicalized (already in tagged-envelope form).

scopeRules.description: Per-effect overrides for how author-side scope shorthand canonicalizes. Most aliases inherit the universal scope canonicalization from common/canonicalization-rules.json.

default.description: Canonical scope to use when the author omits 'scope' entirely.

applyToIsInput.description: When true, author-side 'applyTo' on this effect binds to a per-effect input named 'applyTo' instead of lifting to NodeSpec.writeChannels. Set this on aliases whose descriptors declare applyTo as a real input (e.g., shader.focused_row_gradient where applyTo selects which channel the shader's computed color targets internally). Default behavior (flag absent or false) is the universal lift rule from common/canonicalization-rules.json.

deprecated.description: Free-text note when this alias is being phased out. Canonicalize-time warnings reference this.

since.description: Free-text note when this alias was added (for changelog / docs).

envelope.description: How the author-side value lifts into a canonical ValueSource. 'literal-*' wraps a bare scalar. 'value-source' accepts any of: bare scalar (lifts), $bind:<id> string (becomes Signal), or pre-formed ValueSource object. 'phases-list' accepts a single phase string or array. 'scope-spec' accepts shorthand scope shapes. 'asset-ref' accepts $asset:<id>. 'passthrough' copies the value unchanged (use sparingly).

default.description: Canonical-side default if neither author param nor defaultParams provides a value. Pre-canonicalized.
